- Customer-managed keys: we listed KMS/HSM requirements; need detail on support for external key imports and key churn policies.

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPF questionnaire and DPA annex clarifications

Hi Aria — thanks for the spreadsheet; we reviewed column A and have compiled a short evidence bundle and targeted answers below. Attaching our DPA annex (redwood_dpa_annex_v3.pdf) and a lightweight control matrix to map your statements to evidence (tech-control-matrix.csv).

High-level answers (we will provide deeper evidence for each row in the attached drive link):
1) Cross-border transfers: Redwood supports contractual safeguards (EU SCCs) and the EU-US Data Protection Framework where a customer elects it. For requests where neither is sufficient, we offer several operational controls: regional routing by policy, model routing to EU-only model variants, and ability to restrict inference to Dedicated/Private deployments to avoid US egress. Fallback policy can be set to deny cross-border routing.

2) Customer-managed keys (CMKs): Supported for Dedicated and Private deployments via KMS integration (AWS KMS, Google Cloud KMS) and HSM-backed keys for on-prem. We support external key import for AES/EC keys and key rotation (automatic or manual). Key usage is logged to audit streams; we do not retain plaintext keys.

3) Caching & retention: Prefix/KV caching is optional; cache TTLs are configurable per-route. By default, we do not persist prompt history beyond request logs unless configured by the customer for analytics. Request/response logs are retained per contract and can be set to 30/90/365 days. All logs are accessible via secure audit exports.

4) On-prem package: We have an on-prem appliance bundle and a VPC-private deployment pattern. The checklist is attached in the drive link (includes network ports, storage encryption, KMS integration, and audit log collection).

Next steps: Jordan will provide a technical deep-dive on encryption and runtime isolation; Ben will share SOC 2 evidence and how we deliver artifacts to procurement. If that timeline works we'll upload the evidence pack to the shared drive today and send a DocuSign for the annex.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_dpa_annex_v3.pdf, tech-control-matrix.csv

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Aria Singh <aria.singh@luminexa.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: DPF questionnaire and DPA annex clarifications — technical deep-dive

Aria / team — quick technical responses to the items flagged in column A (point-form so you can map to rows in your spreadsheet):

- Encryption in transit: All control-plane and data-plane traffic uses TLS1.3 with mTLS between Redwood services. For Private deployments we support customer TLS cert termination and internal mTLS.

- Encryption at rest: Data volumes are encrypted with AES-256. In Hosted/Dedicated we use cloud-provider KMS; for Dedicated we can bring-your-own-KMS (BYOK) so you control key material. On-prem supports HSM-backed wallets for FIPS-level separation.

- KMS & key lifecycle: Keys may be rotated on customer schedule. We support key import using standard PKCS#12 / JCEKS flows or cloud KMS import endpoints. Key usage logs include key identifier, operation, caller identity, and timestamp. We do not store private keys outside HSM/KMS.

- Model routing & segmentation: Requests can be routed by policy to region-specific model replicas. In the Hosted plan, model inference may cross regions unless you restrict to EU-only routing; in Dedicated/Private we guarantee locality. For high-assurance cases we recommend Dedicated pools with strict network ACLs.

- Cache/KV retention: KV cache persists only in-memory in default configuration; persistence to fast storage is optional and controlled per-customer. TTL and eviction are configurable. Cached keys are encrypted with a separate cache key that is rotated independently.

- Logging: Redact-able tokens: we provide token-level redaction configs and a built-in scrubber for PII patterns before logs are persisted. Audit log exports include request ids, route, model, token counts, and actors.

- Pen testing & attestations: We run annual third-party penetration tests and provide a redacted pen-test summary under NDA. SOC 2 Type II report available (see Ben's note).

If useful I can export example configuration snippets for KMS integration and the routing policy JSON.

— Jordan
Principal Solutions Engineer
